conventions.convention: A proper Bayesian model includes a specified measurable parameter space, a prior probability, and a sampling probability kernel representing every sampling law pointwise.

A posterior RCD is indexed by sample points; a data-indexed posterior is an everywhere probability kernel satisfying the displayed rectangle identities. Measurable prior-predictive null sets permit fixed-probability replacement.
The general posterior RCD existence route assumes AC and a standard-Borel parameter target; the data space need only be measurable.
The stated general data-indexed existence and simultaneous uniqueness theorem assumes AC and standard-Borel parameter and data spaces.
The countable data index starts at zero: f₀(n)=2^{−(n+1)} and f₁(n)=(2/3)(1/3)^n for n∈N₀.

load_bearing.statement: A proper Bayesian model consists of a prior probability measure Π on the specified parameter measurable space and a probability kernel K representing the experiment: K(θ,B)=Pθ(B) for every θ and data event B.

A posterior RCD is an RCD of X given σ(Y) on any realization with the model's joint law J. The displayed data-indexed characterization requires a probability kernel Πy with Q(X∈A,Y∈B)=∫B Πy(A) QY(dy) for every parameter event A and data event B.

Assume AC. For a proper Bayesian model, on any probability space carrying parameter and data random elements with joint law J, a standard-Borel parameter space ensures existence of a posterior RCD given σ(Y). The data space need only be measurable.

Assume AC and standard-Borel parameter and data spaces in a proper Bayesian model. A data-indexed posterior probability kernel exists, satisfies the joint-law rectangle identity, and composes with Y to give a posterior RCD. Any two such kernels agree as measures outside one measurable data-marginal null set; replacement there by the prior preserves the identities.

concerns.concern: The second paragraph calls the composition “ω↦Π_{Y(ω)}” a “conditional law of X given Y,” citing def-conditional-law-given-a-random-element. That supplier defines the conditional law as a kernel from the data space to the parameter space; its composition with Y is an RCD given σ(Y). The subsequent rectangle characterization is correct and resolves the intended meaning, but the preceding sentence assigns the composition the wrong kernel type.
